steps: Preheat and prep: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Prepare potatoes: If using larger potatoes, cut into 1-inch pieces for even cooking. Place halved baby potatoes in a large pot of salted water. Bring to a boil and cook for 8-10 minutes until just tender when pierced with a fork. Drain well and let steam dry for 2-3 minutes.
Season and toss: In a large bowl, combine drained potatoes, fennel wedges, olive oil, smashed garlic, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Toss until everything is well coated.
Arrange for roasting: Spread vegetables in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, ensuring potatoes are cut-side down for maximum browning. Don't overcrowd.
Roast: Roast for 15 minutes, then carefully flip potatoes and toss fennel. Continue roasting for 12-15 minutes until potatoes are golden brown and crispy, and fennel is caramelized and tender.
Finish and serve: Remove from the oven and sprinkle with chopped fennel fronds and lemon zest. Serve warm.

Spread the beans on a platter. Pile the warm escalivada on top and pour over any roasting juices.
Spoon over the red wine vinegar, scatter the thyme and parsley, and finish with the 2 Tablespoons finishing oil.

title: Escalivada and Mahón Tartines
why: The PDF's main ingredient is 'The reserved escalivada (eggplant and peppers) from Monday', which only makes sense after cooking Monday's recipe; its fallback for cooks who skipped Monday is printed only in the WEDNESDAY PREP notes.
add_ingredients: escalivada (charred eggplant and peppers), reserved from Charred Escalivada over White Beans, or 1 jar roasted red peppers, drained, plus 1 eggplant, quick-broiled about 10 minutes under a hot broiler

title: Marseille Socca and Summer Pistou
why: The pistou is a double batch: half is 'for Wednesday', the Provençal White Beans and Pistou; say so instead of naming the day.
steps: Whisk the chickpea flour, warm water, 2 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper into a smooth batter. Rest 30 minutes.
Pound the basil, garlic, and Parmesan with a pinch of salt, then work in ¼ cup olive oil until loose. If you plan to make Provençal White Beans and Pistou, set half aside in a glass jar for it.
Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a 10-inch cast-iron skillet over medium-high until it shimmers.
Pour in half the batter and tilt to coat. Cook 5 minutes until the edges lift and the underside is browned, then flip and cook 2 minutes more. Repeat with the remaining oil and batter.
Tear the socca into shards and pile onto a platter. Scatter the cherry tomatoes and crumbled chèvre over the top.
Spoon the pistou across the socca and finish with 1 Tbsp olive oil. Serve warm.

title: Provençal White Beans and Pistou
why: Uses pistou set aside in Marseille Socca and Summer Pistou; the PDF's Wednesday prep gives the fallback, pounding a fresh batch.
add_ingredients: reserved basil pistou (set aside from Marseille Socca and Summer Pistou, or pound a fresh batch the same way)

title: Kalamata Bulgur Bowl with Charred Peppers & Olives
why: PDF lists '1 cup bulgur, cooked' and peppers 'charred and sliced' but only its weekly prep guide cooks the bulgur (1 cup dry in 1½ cups vegetable broth, not listed) and chars the peppers; cook time was 0.
steps: Bring the bulgur and broth to a boil in a saucepan. Cover, remove from heat, and let steam 15 minutes, then fluff and spread on a sheet pan to cool.

Meanwhile, char the peppers directly over a gas flame or under the broiler, turning until blackened on all sides, about 8 minutes. Seal in a bowl covered with a plate for 10 minutes, then peel, seed, and slice into strips.
In a large bowl, toss the cooked bulgur with 2 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
Fold in the charred pepper strips, cherry tomatoes, olives, and sliced red onion. Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Arrange all the white beans on top. Drizzle with the finishing 1 Tbsp olive oil.
Serve at room temperature directly from the bowl, family style.

title: Kalamata Chickpeas with Olives and Feta
why: PDF lists 3 oz feta but step 4 and the Thursday prep crumble 1 oz over each of four plates (4 oz).

title: Kolokythokeftedes Zucchini and Feta Fritters
why: PDF lists '2 garlic cloves, minced and divided' plus '1 garlic clove' under a 'For the tzatziki:' heading the app drops, but the steps use only 2 cloves (1 in the batter, 1 in the tzatziki).

title: Pan-seared Sea Bream over Smoky Eggplant
why: PDF lists salt and pepper as divided but the steps never season the fish (only the Tuesday prep box does), so the remaining ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper go unused.
steps: Heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Add eggplant cubes in a single layer. Cook undisturbed 4 minutes, then toss and cook 3 more minutes until golden and tender.

Add onion and garlic. Cook 2 minutes until softened. Stir in tomato paste, capers, and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute. Season with ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.

Wipe the skillet clean. Pat the sea bream dry and season both sides with the remaining ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper. Add 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium-high. When shimmering, add sea bream skin-side down. Press gently with a spatula for 10 seconds. Cook 3 to 4 minutes until skin is crisp. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes until fish reaches 130 to 135°F.
Spoon eggplant mixture onto four plates. Rest a piece of fish on top. Drizzle with lemon juice and finishing 1 Tbsp olive oil. Scatter parsley over.

title: Ligurian Borlotti Beans and Pesto
why: The pesto 'reserved from Monday' is set aside in Ligurian Trofie Al Pesto Genovese; name it.
add_ingredients: 1/3 cup pesto (reserved from Ligurian Trofie Al Pesto Genovese)

title: Ligurian Trofie Al Pesto Genovese
why: PDF reserves 1/3 cup pesto 'for Wednesday' in the last step, after all the pesto was tossed with the pasta; set it aside right after blending and name the recipe it is for.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat.
Add the potatoes and cook for 8 minutes, then add the green beans and cook 4 minutes more.
Add the trofie and cook until tender, about 9 to 11 minutes, then drain and save 1 cup of the water.
Blend the basil, pine nuts, pecorino, garlic, and 3 tablespoons olive oil into a loose pesto. Set aside about 1/3 cup of the pesto for Ligurian Borlotti Beans and Pesto.
Toss the hot pasta and vegetables with the pesto, loosening with a splash of the pasta water.
Finish with 1 tablespoon olive oil, the salt, and the pepper.

title: Alicante Butter Bean Tomato Tartine
why: Beans ingredient says '* see Monday' and the canned-bean fallback is only in the prep list; the 2 Tbsp olive oil (counted in the nutrition) is never used by the steps.
steps: Toast bread slices until golden, about 3 minutes per side.
Rub warm bread with a cut garlic clove, then brush with 2 Tbsp olive oil.
Warm the reserved butter beans in a small skillet over medium, 3 minutes.
Mash beans lightly with a fork and spread over the toasted bread.
Top with sliced tomato, Manchego, salt, and pepper.
Drizzle with 1 Tbsp olive oil and scatter parsley.
add_ingredients: 1½ cups reserved butter beans with sauce, from Alicante Charred Pepper Butter Beans, or one 15-ounce can butter beans warmed with a pinch of smoked paprika

title: Alicante Charred Pepper Butter Beans
why: Step 7 reserves beans 'for Wednesday' (weekly plan); they are for Alicante Butter Bean Tomato Tartine, and the step is optional when this recipe is cooked alone.
steps: Heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a 5-quart Dutch oven over medium.
Add onion and bell peppers. Cook 6 minutes until soft.
Add garlic, smoked paprika, oregano, and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute.
Add cherry tomatoes. Cook 4 minutes until they start to break down.
Add all 3 cans butter beans and vegetable broth. Simmer 12 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper.
If you plan to make Alicante Butter Bean Tomato Tartine, spoon 1½ cups beans with sauce into a glass container. Cool and refrigerate.
Off heat, stir parsley into the remaining beans.
Finish with 1 Tbsp olive oil and serve.

title: Sheet-pan Lemon-herb Chicken Thighs
why: Misprinted page heading: the menu (Friday side) and the page's own nutrition label name this watermelon side 'Chilled Watermelon and Mint Salad', so its printed nutrition was never matched.

title: Crispy Chickpeas over Farro and Radicchio
why: The farro 'reserved from Monday' comes from Ligurian Farro and Kale Braise; name it.
add_ingredients: 1½ cups farro (cooked, reserved from Ligurian Farro and Kale Braise)

title: Ligurian Farro and Kale Braise
why: 'Sunday' is the PDF's weekly prep day; 'ahead' reads on its own. The farro set aside 'for Wednesday' is for Crispy Chickpeas over Farro and Radicchio.
steps: If you cooked the farro ahead, skip to step 3. Otherwise, bring the broth to a boil in a 3-quart saucepan. Add farro, cover, reduce to medium-low, and simmer 25 minutes until tender. Drain any remaining broth.
If you plan to make Crispy Chickpeas over Farro and Radicchio, set aside 1½ cups cooked farro, covered, and refrigerate.
Heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a 5-quart Dutch oven over medium.
Add onion. Cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and rosemary. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and the remaining cooked farro. Simmer 8 minutes.
Add kale in batches, stirring until wilted, about 5 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Off heat, stir in remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil. Top with grated pecorino before serving.

title: Roasted Ligurian Branzino and Chard
why: The PDF line '1 lemon, thinly sliced, plus 1 lemon, juiced (about 2 Tablespoons)' became one lemon; the recipe needs one sliced lemon (step 5) and one juiced lemon (step 7).

title: Gnocchi Niçois and Roasted Squash
why: The squash line only says 'see Monday for recipe': it is the 1 pound set aside in Tian de Courge Niçois Squash Gratin, and the PDF prints its frozen-squash fallback only in the Wednesday prep list.
add_ingredients: 1 pound roasted butternut squash (set aside from Tian de Courge Niçois Squash Gratin; or microwave 1 pound frozen butternut squash cubes for 5 minutes and brown them with the gnocchi)

title: Riviera Lemon Chicken and Braised Leeks
why: Step 6 spoons the leeks 'over the farro', which is the paired side (Warm Épeautre Farro with Parsley and Lemon), not part of this recipe. 'Wednesday night' refers to the weekly plan; 'the night before' reads on its own.
steps: Season chicken on both sides with salt, pepper, and thyme. Skip this step if you dry-brined it the night before.
Warm 2 Tbsp olive oil in a 12-inch braiser or deep skillet over medium-high. Sear chicken 4 minutes per side until browned and transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add leeks and garlic and cook 6 minutes until soft.
Add broth, bay leaf, lemon zest, and olives. Return the chicken, cover, and simmer over medium 18 minutes until it reaches 165°F.
Stir lemon juice into the leeks and discard the bay leaf.
Spoon leeks onto plates (over Warm Épeautre Farro with Parsley and Lemon, if serving), set the chicken on top, and finish with parsley and 1 Tbsp olive oil.

title: Riviera Lemon Leeks and Warm Chèvre
why: Step 5 spoons the leeks and chèvre 'over the farro', which is the paired side (Warm Épeautre Farro with Parsley and Lemon), not part of this recipe.
steps: Warm 2 Tbsp olive oil in a 12-inch ovenproof braiser or deep skillet over medium. Cook leeks, garlic, salt, pepper, and thyme 8 minutes until soft.
Add broth, bay leaf, lemon zest, and olives. Cover and simmer over medium 12 minutes until the leeks are silky.
Stir in lemon juice, discard the bay leaf, and heat the broiler to high.
Set the chèvre rounds over the leeks and broil 3 to 4 minutes until warm and lightly browned.
Spoon the leeks and chèvre onto plates (over Warm Épeautre Farro with Parsley and Lemon, if serving) and finish with parsley and 1 Tbsp olive oil.

title: Tian de Courge Niçois Squash Gratin
why: The squash set aside 'for Wednesday' is for Gnocchi Niçois and Roasted Squash.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss squash with 3 Tbsp olive oil and ½ tsp salt and spread on 2 large, rimmed baking sheets.
Roast 25 minutes, flipping once, until tender and browned at the edges. Reduce oven to 375°F.
If you plan to make Gnocchi Niçois and Roasted Squash, transfer 1 pound roasted squash (about 3 cups) to a glass or silicone container and refrigerate up to 4 days.
Warm 1 Tbsp olive oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium. Cook onion 6 minutes until soft, add garlic, and cook 1 minute.
Lightly mash the remaining squash in a large bowl, leaving some pieces whole.
Whisk in eggs, Parmesan, sage, remaining ½ tsp salt, and pepper, then fold in the onion.
Spread into a parchment-lined 2-quart baking dish and bake at 375°F for 25 minutes until set in the center and golden on top.
Rest 5 minutes, drizzle with 1 Tbsp olive oil, and serve warm from the dish.

title: Mallorcan Eggs in Sofrito and Mushrooms
why: The sofrito line only says 'see Monday for recipe': it is the half set aside in Sopes Mallorquines Chickpea Bread Soup, and the PDF prints its fallback only in the Wednesday prep list.
add_ingredients: 2 cups Mallorcan sofrito (set aside from Sopes Mallorquines Chickpea Bread Soup; or simmer one 14.5-ounce can crushed tomatoes with 1 diced jarred roasted red pepper and 1 teaspoon smoked paprika for 5 minutes)

title: Pebres Torrats Roasted Pepper Salad
why: Step 1 says to broil the peppers 'before heating the oven for the cod', which belongs to the paired main (Peix a la Mallorquina Baked Cod); the vegetarian menu pairs this salad with the butter beans. 'Sunday' is the PDF's weekly prep day; 'ahead' reads on its own.
steps: If you roasted the peppers ahead, skip to step 4. Otherwise, heat broiler on high. Broil peppers on a rimmed baking sheet 6 inches from the heat for 15 minutes, turning every 5 minutes, until blackened on all sides.
Transfer to a bowl, cover, and steam 10 minutes.
Peel, seed, and slice the peppers into ½-inch strips over the bowl to catch the juices.
Toss peppers and juices with olive oil, garlic, vinegar, and salt. Rest 10 minutes at room temperature.
Top with capers and parsley before serving.

title: Sopes Mallorquines Chickpea Bread Soup
why: The sofrito set aside 'for Wednesday' is for Mallorcan Eggs in Sofrito and Mushrooms.
steps: Heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a 5-quart Dutch oven over medium. Add onions and red peppers and cook 12 minutes, stirring often, until soft and sweet.
Add garlic and smoked paprika and cook 1 minute. Add tomatoes and salt and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
If you plan to make Mallorcan Eggs in Sofrito and Mushrooms, transfer half the sofrito (about 2 cups) to a glass container, cool, and refrigerate up to 4 days.
Add leeks and chard stems to the pot and cook over medium 5 minutes until the leeks soften.
Add chickpeas, broth, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium 12 minutes.
Stir in chard leaves and simmer 3 minutes until wilted. Remove the bay leaf.
Divide the dried bread among four wide bowls and ladle the soup over it. Rest 2 minutes so the bread softens.
Top with parsley and drizzle with 1 Tbsp olive oil, for finishing.

title: Spinach Pear and Toasted Almond Salad
why: 'Sunday' is the PDF's weekly prep day; 'ahead' reads on its own.
steps: If you toasted the almonds ahead, just chop them. Otherwise, toast almonds in a 10-inch skillet over medium 5 minutes, shaking the pan. Cool and roughly chop.
Whisk vinegar, salt, and pepper in a large bowl, then whisk in olive oil.
Add spinach and pear and toss to coat.
Top with Manchego and almonds and serve right away.

title: Patates Lemonates Greek Lemon Potatoes
why: Step 4 ends with 'Slide the sfougato in for the last 15 minutes', a step of the paired main (Leek and Mushroom Sfougato Baked Omelet).
steps: Heat oven to 400°F.
Toss potatoes with oil, lemon zest and juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish. Tuck in rosemary.
Pour broth around the potatoes.
Roast at 400°F 45 minutes, turning once at 25 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the edges are browned.
Spoon pan juices over the potatoes and serve.
